data: 私[わたし]に とって 何[なに]よりも 大切[たいせつ]なのは、 家族[かぞく]の 幸[しあわ]せです。
What's more important to me than anything else is my family's happiness.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
私[わたし]が 取[と]っているのは、 中国[ちゅうごく]語[ご]では なくて 日本[にほん]語[ご]です。
What I'm taking is Japanese, not Chinese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that a certain piece of information is wrong and, following that, to present the correct information. ではなく(て) is used in written language and じゃなく(て) is used in spoken language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not A, but B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) N2 b. Phrase1 {では/じゃ}なく(て) Phrase2
両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に、 いつも 早[はや]く 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]ってくる ように 言[い]います。
My parents always tell me to come home early. (Indirect Quote)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
今[いま]、 私[わたし]が 住[す]んでいる アパートの 広[ひろ]さは、 この 部屋[へや]と 同[おな]じぐらいです。
Right now, the apartment I'm living in is about the same size as this room.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
私[わたし]は 来週[らいしゅう]、 学校[がっこう]の 代表[だいひょう]と して スピーチ コンテストに 出[で]ます。
Next week, I'm participating in a speech contest as the representative from my school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: として is used to indicate the role, capacity, or occupation of someone or the function or characteristics of something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: as; in the capacity of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nとして1
私[わたし]の 大学[だいがく]の チームは 試合[しあい]に 出[で]る たびに、 負[ま]けてしまう。 もっと 強[つよ]くなってほしいなあ。
My university's team loses every match they have. I whish they'd get better.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past たびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
A) ロボットが 作[つく]った 商品[しょうひん]を、 ここで 私[わたし]たち チェック するんです。 B） あー、 最後[さいご]に チェック するのは、 やっぱり 人間[にんげん]な わけですね。
A) This is where we check the products that the robots have produced. B) Oh, so it's humans who do a final check after all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

~わけだ。 Means: The reason is that~; it means that~; that's why~; no wonder~; naturally Can be used in 3 situations, here it is (2) when a speaker reaches a logical conclusion based on what he/she has learned from the hearer or has discovered.
週末[しゅうまつ]は、 勉強[べんきょう] 以外[いがい]に、 テニスを したり 映画[えいが]を 見[み]たり します。
Besides studying, I do things like play tennis and watch movies on the weekend.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.
日本[にほん]の 有名[ゆうめい]な 小説[しょうせつ]が ハリウッドで 映画[えいが]化[か] される ことに なった。
It's been decided that that famous novel will be adapted for the screen.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
残念[ざんねん]な ことに、 私[わたし]達[たち]の チームは 最後[さいご]の 試合[しあい]で 負[ま]けてしまった。
Unfortunately, our team lost in the last match.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa なことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
私[わたし]の 家[いえ]では 食事[しょくじ]の 後[あと]、 自分[じぶん]が つかった お皿[さら]を 洗[あら]う ことに なっている。
At my house, the rule is that you wash your own place after a meal.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
田中[たなか]さんも あの 映画[えいが]、 見[み]たんですか？ 私[わたし]も 先週[せんしゅう] 見[み]たんですよ。 とっても 良[よ]かったでしょう。
You saw that movie, Mr. Tanaka? I saw it last week, too. Wasn't it great?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
私[わたし]の 国[くに]では 日本[にほん]に 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く 時[とき]、 旅行[りょこう] ビザを 取[と]る 必要[ひつよう]は ない。
As for my country, when traveling to Japan it is not necessary to get a travel Visa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This phrase is used to indicate the necessity of doing something. は is common with a negative ending. --- 英訳 [English translation]: a. V必要がある = It is necessary to V; must V; have to V. b. V必要はない = It is not necessary to V; there is no need to V; don't have to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past 必要{がある/はない}
私[わたし]は 旅行[りょこう]が 大好[だいす]きで 世界[せかい]中[じゅう]を 旅行[りょこう] した。 南極[なんきょく] （へ/に）さえ 行[い]った ことが ある。
I love traveling and I've traveled all over the world. I've even been to Antarctica.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
私[わたし]が 住[す]んでいる アパートは、 周[まわ]りが 静[しず]かなだけでなく 安全[あんぜん]でも あるので、 学生[がくせい]に 人気[にんき]が ある。
The apartment I'm living in is in an area that's not just quiet; it's also safe, so it's popular among students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
あの 映画[えいが]は 面白[おもしろ]い はずだよ。 映画[えいが] 先行[せんこう]の 友達[ともだち]が 3[さん]回[かい]も 見[み]たって 言[い]ってたから。
That movie must be interesting because my friend majoring in film studies told me that he'd seen it three times.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.
私[わたし]は この 教科[きょうか]書[しょ]が 大好[だいす]きだ。 何[なに]より、 単語[たんご]と 漢字[かんじ]が 覚[おぼ]えやすいと いうのが いい。
I love this textbook. More than anything else, the way it makes it easy to remember vocabulary and kanji is good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
何より（も） "before everything; above all; first of all; more than anything else; the most ~"
私[わたし]は 日本[にほん] 文学[ぶんがく]を 研究[けんきゅう] したいと 思[おも]っている。だが、 両親[りょうしん]は 私[わたし]に 医者[いしゃ]に なってほしがっている。
I think I'd like to study Japanese literature. My parents, however, want me to become a doctor.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1. だが、S2. "but; however" だが is a disjunctive conjunction. S1 and S2 present contrastive statements or opposing ideas. Note: でも、けれど、けど are colloquial けれども、しかしながら、だが、and が are primarily used in written language. しかし can be used in both written and spoken language.
両親[りょうしん]は 毎日[まいにち]の ように、 よく 勉強[べんきょう] していい 大学[だいがく]に 入[はい]りなさいと 言[い]います。 それなら、 私[わたし]が 勉強[べんきょう] している とき、 弟[おとうと]や 妹[いもうと]に 静[しず]かにする ように 言[い]ってほしいと 思[おも]います。
My parents tell me almost every day to study hard so I can get into a good university. If that's what they want, I want them to tell my little brother and sister to be quiet while I'm studying.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
それなら "If that's the case; If so" それ meaning "that" refers to the speaker's previous statement of the statement which was just made by the hearer.
田中[たなか] 先生[せんせい]の 研究[けんきゅう]室[しつ]には、 百[ひゃく]年[ねん] 以上[いじょう] 前[まえ]の 辞書[じしょ]も あれば、 最近[さいきん]の 映画[えいが]の DVDも ある。
In Professor Tanaka's office there are dictionaries from more than a hundred years ago as well as DVDs of recent films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
今週[こんしゅう]中[ちゅう]に メールを 出[だ]すか 電話[でんわ]を 掛[か]けるか しますから、 待[ま]っていて下[くだ]さい。
I'll either e-mail you or call you some time this week, so please wait for that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]になる 地[ち] つれて、 日本[にほん]人[じん]と 話[はな]すのが 静[しずか] 香[かぐわ]しくなくなってきた。
As my Japanese improves, I've become less embarrassed when talking with Japanese people.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-non-past.aff につれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
高[たか]い レストランだから おいしいとは 限[かぎ]らない。
It's not always true that expensive restaurants serve good food.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
〜とは限らない "not necessarily~; not always ~; it's not necessarily the case that~" Xとは限らない means "it's not necessarily the case that X." だ before とは is optional.
本当[ほんとう]である 限[かぎ]り 本当[ほんとう]でない 限[かぎ]り
As long as it's true... As long as it isn't true...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANoで {ある／ない} V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
この 留学[りゅうがく] プログラムは、 ホームステイが できると いう 点[てん]が、 セールス ポイントですね。
The fact that this study abroad program provides students with the opportunity to do a homestay is one of its selling points, isn't it?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {という/の} 点で (は） "in terms of ~; with regard to ~; with respect to ~" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."
今[いま]、 どこの 大学[だいがく]に 留学[りゅうがく] してたっけ？
Where is the University that you are studied abroad at now?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.past (んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
マイクさん、 今[いま]、 どこの 大学[だいがく]に 留学[りゅうがく] してたっけ？
(I forget…) What was the name of the university where Mike's doing his study abroad?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.past (んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
ゆうべ 飲[の]み過[す]ぎた せいで、 朝[あさ]から 頭[あたま]が ガンガン する。
I drank too much alst night, so my head has been throbbing since this morning.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain せい "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
この 製品[せいひん]に 使[つか]われている ものは、 何[なに]から 何[なに]まで リサイクル できます。
Every single part of this product can be recycled.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
何から何まで "all; anything and everything; all kinds" 何から何まで means "all" and is more emphatic than 全部, すべて、or みんな. 何から何まで can be used with 全部、みんな、and すべて。
オリンピックを する ことに 決[き]まってから、 その 国[くに]は 国際[こくさい]的[てき]になってきた。
After it was decided that it would host the Olympics, that country has become more cosmopolitan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
富士[ふじ]山[やま]の 高[たか]さは 何[なん]キロくらいでしょうか。
About how many kilometers is the height of Mt. Fuji, I wonder.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
病状[びょうじょう]に 合[あ]わせて、 いろいろな 薬[くすり]が 使[つか]われる。
A variety of medicines are used depending on the condition of the patient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に会わせて "making ~ suitable for N; according to N" The literal meaning this grammar is "fitting/matching/adjusting something to N" and is often used to mean "making something suitable for N" or "according to N"
それぞれの 国[くに]には、 それぞれの 文化[ぶんか]や 習慣[しゅうかん]が ある。
Each country has it's own culture and traditions.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
それぞれ のN Means: each; one's own; in one's own way それぞれ is used to focus on each individual or thing in a group of people or things, and means "each (one of them)."
だいたいの 数[かず]は 分[わ]かりますが、 正確[せいかく]な 数[かず]は 調[しら]べてみないと 分[わ]かりません。
We have approximate figures, but we'll have to do some research to get an accurate count.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だいたい number/amount "approximately number/amount" だいたい means "most;almost; nearly(all); approximate." The meaning changes depending on what だいたい modifies.
この 情報[じょうほう]を 見[み]るには、 この ソフトウェアを インストール する 必要[ひつよう]が あります。
In order to view this information, it is necessary to install this software.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past.aff には "to; in order to; for; for the purpose of; when" には indicates purpose in general statements (often stating the speaker's judgement about an action in terms of its effectiveness, convenience, necessity, etc.). には can also mean "when" (=時には). Verbs or nouns can precede には. Note that when ために is used, the predicate in the main clause describes an action. Such that: Xには Y, where Y is a judgment and never an action XためにY, where Y is an action and never a judgement. AND, XためにはY, where Y is a judgment, never an action
ハイブリッドの 車[くるま]が 増[ふ]えた ことに よって、 町[まち]の 空気[くうき]が きれい なってきました。
Because hybrid cars increased, the city's air came to be cleaner.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~ことによって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates CAUSE. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
プレイスメント テストに 合格[ごうかく] しない 限[かぎ]り、 上[うえ]の レベルの クラスには 入[い]れません。
You won't be able to take upper-level classes until you pass the placement test.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
指示[しじ] 通[どお]りに、 ここに 答[こた]えを 書[か]いて下[くだ]さい。
Please write your answers here as indicated by the instructions.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N通り（に） Where 通り is a suffix and reads as どおり。 "the way; as; exactly like; following; according to" When 通り is modified by a verb or noun, it means "the way; as someone does; as something indicates." 通り can also be used as a suffix, in which case 通り is directly affixed to nouns and the pronunciation changes from とおり to どおり。
東京[とうきょう]の 物価[ぶっか]は ニューヨークと 同[おな]じぐらい 高[たか]い。
Prices in Tokyo are about as high as they are in New York.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The particle ぐらい/くらい "approximately" often occurs with 同じ to mean "about the same." --- 英訳 [English translation]: about as ~ as; about the same ~ as ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N と同じ{ぐらい/くらい} b. N1 と同じ{ぐらい/くらい}の N2
授業[じゅぎょう]に 関係[かんけい]の ない 質問[しつもん]は しない ようにしましょう。
Try not to ask questions that are not related to the lesson.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 {と/に} 関係 {が/の} あるN2. This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。
留学[りゅうがく] すると いうのは、 外国[がいこく]で 勉強[べんきょう] すると いう ことだ。
Ryuugakusuru means to study in a foreign country.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The structure ~というのは~だ is used to provide the meaning or definition of a word or phrase. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X means ~; The meaning of X is ~; What X means is ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. ~ というのは {Nのこと / N ということ}だ b. ~ というのは Sことだ. Type 2c c. ~ というのは {Sということ/Sという意味}だ. Type 1
来年[らいねん]は、 少[すく]なくとも 3[みっ]つは 授業[じゅぎょう]を 取[と]らなければいけない。
Next year, I have to take at least three classes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
少なくとも N (は） 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number. When used with a noun, は often follows the noun (or the particle after the noun), indicating that the noun is under focus.
ウィキペディアの こと 人物[じんぶつ]に 関[かん]する 情報[じょうほう]は 正[ただ]しくない ようだ。
It seems that the information Wikipedia has on this person is incorrect.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 に関する N2 formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to"
レオナルド・ ダ・ビンチは 芸術[げいじゅつ]家[か]でも あり、 科学[かがく]者[しゃ]でも あった。
Leonardo da Vinci was a scientiest as well as an artist.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N／ANa でもある "be also" X は Y でもある. OR X は Y でもあり、Z でもある。 Are used to introduce another property of X when X has more than one property.
現代[げんだい]人[じん]に とって、 コンピュータの ない 生活[せいかつ]は 考[かんが]えられないだろう。
I feel that life without computers is unthinkable to people today.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N {は／なんて} 考えられない "unimaginable; inconceivable; unthinkable"
レポートは 一応[いちおう] 書[か]き上[あ]げたけれど、 英語[えいご]の スペル チェックが まだだ。

この 映画[えいが]は 子供[こども]でも 子供[こども] {じゃ/で} なくても、 楽[たの]しめます。
Whether you're a kid or not, you can enjoy this film.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/ANo/N} でも {ANa/ANo/N} {じゃ／で} なくても "whether X or not"
先生[せんせい]の 言[い]った こと、 ノートに 書[か]いとかないと、 忘[わす]れちゃうよ。
If you don't write down what the professor says, you end up forgetting it, you know.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
In casual conversation contracted forms are commonly used.
おいしい 料理[りょうり]だったが、 お腹[なか]が 痛[いた]くて ほとんど 食[た]べられなかった。

ほとんど〜ない。 means: hardly (ever); rarely; almost no(thing)
私[わたし]は 技術[ぎじゅつ]な ことは よく わからないので、 ほかの 人[ひと]に 聞[き]いてください。
I don't understand technological things very well, so you should ask someone else.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
将来[しょうらい]は、 ヨーロッパ、 あるいは、 アジアで 仕事[しごと]が できたらいいと 思[おも]っている。
I think it'd be nice if I can work in Europe or Asia in the future.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
現代[げんだい]は、 コンピューターが なければ、 暮[く]らしにくい 時代[じだい]に なったと 言[い]えるだろう。
One could say that we've entered an era where it's hard to live without computers.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used when the speaker is quite certain that his/her statement is correct but wants to soften the statement so as not to appear too assertive. This is a formal expression. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It probably can be said that ~; it is probably all right to say that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と言えるだろう
道子[みちこ]さんの 出身[しゅっしん]って、 何処[どこ]?
Where are you from, Michiko? / Where's Michiko from?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って
1[いち]年[ねん]に 700万[ななれいれいまん]人[にん] 以上[いじょう]の 人[ひと]が 訪[おとず]れると いう。
It is said over 7 million visit each year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という "It is said that ~; They say that ~" This structure indicate that the preceding information is not first hand. This is a polite form.
昨夜[さくや]から 今朝[けさ]に かけて、 たくさん 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]った。
We had lots of rain from last night through this morning.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 から N2 にかけて "from N1 to N2" indicates a span of time or space and is used primarily in written language.
この 漢字[かんじ] 何[なん]回[かい] 覚[おぼ]えても、 すぐに 忘[わす]れてしまう。
No matter how many times I memorize this kanji I forget it right away.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ても is used with a question word, the phrase means: "no matter" or "without regard to." --- 英訳 [English translation]: no matter what/who/when/where/how --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ QW(prt)+V-teも
これは 敬語[けいご]の 使[つか]い方[かた]を 練習[れんしゅう] する ための サイトだ。
This is a site created to help people practice their keigo.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
古代[こだい]の ヨーロッパは ローマを 中心[ちゅうしん]と して 発展[はってん] した。
Ancient Europe developed with Rome at its center.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N を 中心 {と/に} (して） "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." Nを中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify verbs. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
アラビア語[ご]は 最[もっと]も 難[むずか]しい 言葉[ことば]の 一[ひと]つだと 言[い]われています。
It is said that Arabic is one of the hardest languages to learn.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to describe X while indicating that X is not the only example, object, person, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is one of the ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ NはNPの{一つ/一人}だ。
電車[でんしゃ]に 乗[の]ろうと したら、 目[め]の 前[まえ]で ドアが 閉[し]まってしまった。
Just as I was about to get on the train, the doors closed before my eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
今年[ことし]は あまり 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]らない。 その ために スキーが 出来[でき]ない。
There hasn't been much snow this year. Because of that, we can't go skiing.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)
田中[たなか]さんが 昨日[きのう] 着[き]ていた ような、 あんな シャツが 欲[ほ]しいなあ。
I want a shirt like the one Mr. Tanaka was wearing yesterday.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
この 間[あいだ]の 試験[しけん]は かなり 難[むずか]しかったが、 いい 点[てん]を 取[と]る ことが できた。
The last test was pretty hard, but I did well on it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
郵便[ゆうびん] 局[きょく]に 行[い]って来[こ]なくちゃん ないから、 ちょっと ここで 待[ま]ってて。
I've gotta run to the post office, so wait here for a sec.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
雨[あめ]が 強[つよ]く 降[ふ]ってきたにも かかわらず、 サッカーの 試合[しあい]は 続[つづ]けられた。
Despite the fact that it began to rain hard, the soccer match continued.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

X にもかかわらず Y where X is {V/A}-plain ANa {な／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} N {の／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} "in spite of (the fact that ~); despite (the fact that ~); although; though; nevertheless" This construction is used to mean "Y in spite of X." It is used when Y is the case even though Y is not usually expected from X.
この 大学[だいがく]の ビジネス学[がく] 部[ぶ]は、 医学[いがく] 部[ぶ]と 並[なら]んでは いるのが 難[むずか]しいらしい。
I hear that the business school at this university, just like the medical school, is hard to get into.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
この 論文[ろんぶん]は すばらしいと 思[おも]う。 しかしながら、 賛成[さんせい] できない 点[てん]も いくつか ある。
I think this is an excellent paper. However, there are a few points with which I cannot agree.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. しかしながら S2. "however, but" しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is used typically in written language.
田中[たなか]さんから メールの 返事[へんじ]が できない。 送[おく]った はずの メールが 届[とど]かなかった ようだ。
Mr. Tanaka hasn't replied to my e-mail. I'm sure I sent it, but it looks like it didn't reach him.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.
朝[あさ]から 晩[ばん]まで コンピュータの スクリーンを 見[み]続[つづ]けているので、 目[め]が 悪[わる]くなってしまった。
I'm continuously looking at a computer screen from morning till night, so my eyes have gotten bad.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 続く Means: continue to; continue V-ing; go on V-ing; keep (on) V-ing;all the way; all the time This phrase is used when the subject continues doing something volitionally.
この アパートは 家賃[やちん]が 安[やす]いから、 静[しず]かでも 静[しず]か {じゃ/で} なくても、 借[か]りようと 思[おも]っています。
The rent for this apartment is cheap, so whether it's quiet or not I'm thinking about renting it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/ANo/N} でも {ANa/ANo/N} {じゃ／で} なくても "whether X or not"
経済[けいざい]は 政治[せいじ]と 深[ふか]い 関係[かんけい]が ある。
Economics is profoundly related to politics.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 は N2 {と／に}関係がある。 This sentence is used to show that N1 is related in someway to N2. The particle after N1 may be と or に。 When this pattern is used in relative clauses, の is commonly used after 関係 instead of が。
今[いま]の ままだと、 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]は 止[と]まらない。
If things keep going like this, global warming won't come to an end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のままだ "remain the same as ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
漢字[かんじ]が 難[むずか]しいと 思[おも]っている 学生[がくせい]は 少[すく]なくない。
There are more than a few students who think that kanji are difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.
面白[おもしろ]くて 元気[げんき]が 出[で]る、 そう いう 本[ほん]を 探[さが]しています。
Something interesting and invigorating - that's the kind of book I'm looking for.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
この ゲームは、 子供[こども]でも 大人[おとな]でも 楽[たの]しむ ことが 出来[でき]ます。
Everyone from children to adults can enjoy this game.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
とうとう 博士[はかせ] 論文[ろんぶん]が 完成[かんせい] した。 5[ご]年[ねん]も かかってしまった。
My doctoral dissertation is finally complete. It took me five whole years.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

とうとう V "finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all" とうとう indicates that an expected situation has occurred after an extended period of time. The adverb ついに is similar to とうとう and can be used in the place of とうとう. ついに is more formal.
この 文法[ぶんぽう]は 難[むずか]しいと 言[い]っても、 全部[ぜんぶ] 分[わ]からない わけでは ない。
Although I say that this grammar is difficult, that doesn't mean I don't understand it at all.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain {と/って} 言っても "although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~" Its used to clarify what has just been said in order to avoid misunderstanding. って is used in place of と in casual conversation or writing.
私[わたし]の 血液[けつえき]型[がた]は Ａです、 母[はは]は ＡＢ型[がた]で 父[ちち]は Ｏ型[がた]、 弟[おとうと]は Ｂ型[がた]です。
My blood type is A, but my mother's is AB, my father's is O, and my little brother's is B.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 型 is a suffix meaning "style, type, model, etc." It is commonly used to describe the shape, type, model, or newness of an object. The preceding elements are mostly nouns, but some adjectival kanji characters can also precede 型(e.g. 大, 新, 薄). --- 英訳 [English translation]: style; type; pattern; make; model; design --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2
私[わたし]に とって、 読[よ]み物[もの]が 難[むずか]しいか どうかは、 漢字[かんじ]の 多[おお]さに よります。
As it concerns me, whether I find reading material difficult or not depends on the "numerousness" of the kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
できれば 医者[いしゃ]に なりたいが、 授業[じゅぎょう]料[りょう]が 高[たか]いので 難[むずか]しいかも しれない。
If possible, I would like to become a doctor, but the tuition cost is expensive so it'll probably be difficult to do.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase literally means "if possible." It is also used when the speaker asks a favor of someone in a less direct way. できれば is slightly more formal than できたら. --- 英訳 [English translation]: if possible; if you don't mind; if it's all right --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ できれば／できたら
アラビア語[ご]は、 日本[にほん]語[ご]や ロシア語[ご]と 並[なら]んで 難[むずか]しい 言葉[ことば]だと 言[い]われている。
Arabic, along with languages like Japanese and Russian, is said to be a difficult language to learn.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N と並んで "as well as; just like" Is used when introducing one or more examples to be compared to the subject of the sentence. It is used primarily in written language.
私[わたし]は 健康[けんこう]の ため、 エレベーターに 乗[の]らないで 階段[かいだん]を 使[つか]う ことに しています。
To maintain my health, I make a habit of taking the stairs instead of the elevator.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit, as seen in the example sentence in this flashcard. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
この アパートは 駅[えき]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]な ことは 便利[べんり]だけれど、 家賃[やちん]は とても 高[たか]いです。
It's true that this apartment is close to the station and is convenient, but the rent is really high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {な/だった} ことは ANa {だ/だった} が "It is certainly true that ~, but; indeed ~, but; do V ~, but; ~ is/are/was/etc. ~, but" This structure is used when the speaker/writer admits that the proposition is true but wants to qualify the proposition with an additional remark.
赤[あか]ちゃんが 泣[な]いてばかり いるので、 母親[ははおや]に なったばかりの 洋子[ようこ]さんは とても 困[こま]っている。
The baby cries all the time, so Yoko, who has just become a mother, is at it wits' end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−te ばかりいる。 Means: Nothing But; always; all the time ばかり is used to express the idea that someone does one thing all the time and does nothing else, or that someone chooses just one thing among others when doing something. Ex: 田中さんはマンガばかり読んでいる。 can mean: (= All tanaka does is read comics); (= Tanaka reads only comics); (=When Masao reads, he reads nothing but comics) NOTE: ばっかり is more colloquial than ばかり
受付[うけつけ]の 仕事[しごと]は 一応[いちおう] 私[わたし]達[たち]が やる ことに なっています。
We're supposed to work at the reception desk for the time being.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "for the time being" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
これは、 私[わたし]の 子供[こども]の 時[とき]の 経験[けいけん]を もとに した 小説[しょうせつ]です。
This is a novel I wrote based on my elementary school experiences.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: をもとにして is a compound particle meaning "based on."して here is optional. The noun-modification form is をもとにした. --- 英訳 [English translation]: based on --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをもとに(して) N1をもとにしたN2
子供[こども]達[たち]が 幸[しあわ]せな 人生[じんせい]が 送[おく]れる ようにと 願[ねが]っています。
I hope that the children can be sent a happy life.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain.nonpast ように（と）願う Means: hope that ~ And is used to express the speaker's hope or desire that what is stated in the sentence will become a reality.
毎月[まいつき] もらう 給料[きゅうりょう]の うち、 2[に]割[わり]は 家賃[やちん]の ために 使[つか]います。
Twenty percent of my monthly salary goes towards paying rent.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のうち(で) "in; of; among" Xのうち(で）is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
洋風[ようふう]の ホテルも 和風[わふう]の 温泉[おんせん] 旅館[りょかん]も、 どちらも 好[す]きです。
I like Western-style hotels as well as Japanese-style inns with hot springs.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 風の N2 "~style; ~type; look like" 風 is a suffix and is added to nouns to make no-adjectives. X風 means "X style/type" or "looks like X"
最近[さいきん]、 子供[こども]に よる ケータイの 使[つか]い過[す]ぎが 問題[もんだい]に なっている。
Recently, the overuse of cell phones by children has become a problem.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N/NP が問題に {される／なる} "X becomes an issue; X is brought up as an issue; X is questioned; X is called into question." X を 問題にする means "to bring X up as an issue" or "to question X." This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.
アジアに おける 歴史[れきし]に 関[かん]する 問題[もんだい]は、 解決[かいけつ]が 難[むずか]し そうです。
Resolving the disputes in Asia regarding history looks difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 における N2 "in;at;on;during" The compound particle における indicate the place or time of an action, event, or state. The pre-verbal form is において. Both are used only in formal language.
2[に]年[ねん]生[せい]の 日本[にほん]語[ご]より 3[さん]年[ねん]生[せい]の 日本[にほん]語[ご]の ほうが 簡単[かんたん]な 気[き]が する。
I feel like third-year Japanese is easier than second-year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

~(ような）気がする Meaning; I feel that~: I have a feeling that ~; have the impression that ~; it seems to me that~ It indicates that the speaker is not certain about something, but has the feeling that it's true. ような can be dropped without changing the meaning.
私[わたし]が 重[おも]い 病気[びょうき]だと いう ことは、 両親[りょうしん]を 除[のぞ]いて だれも 知[し]らない。
Aside from my parents, no one knows that I have a serious disease.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N を除いて "except (for); with the exception of ~; but ~" 除く means "to remove; get rid of." を除いて is used as a compound particle meaning "except."
母[はは]が 病気[びょうき]だったので、 （母[はは]の） 代[か]わりに 私[わたし]が 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を 作[つく]りました。
Because mom was ill, I made dinner instead.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: の代わりに is used to present something/someone that is replacing or has replaced something/someone. When the context is clear, Noun の can be omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in place of; instead of; to make up for --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nの代わりに
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の 問題[もんだい]は もっと 大[おお]きくなっていくのでは ないでしょうか。
I think that the problem of global warming may grow bigger from now on.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
明日[あした]は 他[た]の 約束[やくそく]が あるから、 行[い]かないって 言[い]ったでしょ。 忘[わす]れたの？
I told you that I've already got plans, so I can't go. Did you forget?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
将来[しょうらい]は、 宇宙[うちゅう]にも 人間[にんげん]が 住[す]める ようになるだろうと 考[かんが]えられている。
It is thought that in the future humans may be able to live even in outer space.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S と考えられている and S と思われている is used to introduce a generally-accepted opinion regarding some matter. 考えられている usually indicates an opinion arrived at through logic, and 思われている usually indicates an opinion derived from intuition. Note that S と考えられている and S と思われている indicates the speaker/writer's opinion. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It is believed that~; It is considered that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S-plain と{考えられている/思われている}
調査[ちょうさ]に よると、 この 大学[だいがく]での 大学[だいがく]院[いん]生[せい]の 割合[わりあい]は 25[にじゅうご]％と なっています。
According to the survey, it turns out that 25% of this university's student population are graduate students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

AはBとなっている。 where B = Noun or noun equivalent such as "# + counter" or "N + Prt" Meaning: happen to be; it turns out that ~; it's been decided that~; the rule is that ~ indicates that what is stated in the preceding AはB sentence is something beyond the speaker's control. The sentence is often findings or matters decided by others. Note that だ does not occur after B in the sentence.
図書[としょ]館[かん]で 1[いち]時間[じかん]ぐらい かかって、 ついに その 本[ほん]を 探[さが]し出[だ]した 時[とき]は、 うれしかった。
I was happy when I finally found the book after spending about an hour at the library searching for it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (2) Someone begins something or something begins
子供[こども]が 10[じゅう]人[にん] います。 ミカンは 30[さんじゅっ]個[こ] ありますから、 一人[ひとり]当[あ]たり 何[なん]個[こ] 食[た]べられますか。
There are then children. We have thirty tangerines, so how many can each child eat?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

number+counter当たりのN Means: per~; a ~; for a ~説明 [explanation]: 当たり is used with ー (or 1) and a counter to mean "per." Sometimes numbers other than one are used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: per~; a ~; for a ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number + Counter 当たり Number + Counter b. Number + Counter 当たりの N
2007[にせんなな]年[ねん]の 夏[なつ]、 子供[こども]達[たち]は ついに ハリー ポッターの 最後[さいご]の ストーリーを 読[よ]む ことが できた。
At last, in the summer of 2007, children were able to read the final installment of the Harry Potter series.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The adverb ついに indicates that something happens or something expected doesn't happen, after waiting for it, longing for it, expecting it to happen, making an effort to make it happen, or after struggling/suffering in a hard situation for a long time. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at last; finally; in the end; after all --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ついに
「すごい」や 「かわいい」などは、 若[わか]い 人[ひと]達[たち]が よく 使[つか]う 表現[ひょうげん]だ。 (=～などと いう 言葉[ことば]は)
Words like "awesome" or "cute" are expressions often used by young people.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) Sentence など(は) is an abbreviated form of S などということは, which means "things like S." (2) Noun など(は) is a shortened form of Noun などという{もの/人/etc.}は, which means "things/people/etc. like N." なんで is a colloquial version of など(は). (3) When S is a quotation, Sなどと is an abbreviated form of S などということを. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/people/etc. like ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N{など(は)/なんて}: 子供{など(は)/なんて}
アパートは 駅[えき]に 近[ちか]ければ 近[ちか]いほど 家賃[やちん]が 高[たか]くなり、 逆[ぎゃく]に、 駅[えき]から 遠[とおざ]ければ 遠[とお]いほど 安[やす]くなる。
The closer an apartment is to the train station to more expensive rent becomes. Inversely, the farther an apartment is from the train stations, the cheaper it becomes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-cond {V/A}-plain ほど "the (more) ~, the (more) ~" This structure is used when the more something happens or is in some state, the more another thing happens or is in some state. (When V is a suru verb, the second VN is usually omitted)
へえ。 日本[にほん]では 四国[しこく]に 住[す]んでおられたんですか。 暖[あたた]かいし、 海[うみ]も きれいだし、 いい 所[ところ]ですよね。
Wow, you lived in Shikoku when you were in Japan? It's a nice place, isn't it? The weather's warm and the sea's beautiful, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

る-verbs: V-masu + られる Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。 sentence final よね indicates the speaker is unsure about the statement.
電車[でんしゃ]の ドアが 開[ひら]くと 同時[どうじ]に、 多[おお]くの 人[ひと]が 降[お]りて来[き]た。
People poured out of the train as soon as the doors opened.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{V/A}-plain.non-pastと同時に "as soon as; the moment; at the same time; also; as well"
最近[さいきん]の 子供[こども]は、 外[そと]で 遊[あそ]ばない 上[うえ]に 本[ほん]も 読[よ]まないらしい。
They say that children these days not only don't play outdoors, they don't even read books.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S 上に "in addition to~; besides~; not only~but also~; moreover~; ~ as well" The conjunction 上に introduces additional information emphatically.
子供[こども]の うちに 外国[がいこく] 語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] すると 発音[はつおん]が よくなる そうだ。
If you study foreign languages while you're still a child you can develop good pronunciation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
私[わたし]は この 仕事[しごと]が 終[お]わらない 限[かぎ]り、 家[いえ]に 帰[かえ]る ことが 出来[でき]ない。
Until this job is finished, I can't return home.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 宿題[しゅくだい]は 今晩[こんばん] しますが、 後[あと]に 宿題[しゅくだい]は 明日[あした] する つもりです。
I'm going to do my Japanese homework tonight, but I'll do the rest of my homework tomorrow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

後のN "the remaining ~; the remainder of ~; the rest of ~" This use of 後 should be distinguished from 後 in the following example, where 後 means "~more." In this use, の cannot occur after 後. このプロジェクトには後三人必要だ。
